I'm responding to your comment: after paying €170 for your visit for an ulcer (plus the eye drops at the pharmacy), I called veterinarians who confirmed that the Acular eye drops you gave me are NOT enough to heal an ulcer on their own. Today, another ophthalmologist saw Kali. Not only has the ulcer not healed at all, but the ophthalmologist told me to stop the Acular eye drops immediately because they help with the pain but are not useful for healing an ulcer. He prescribed two other eye drops (including Vigamox, which I myself insisted on two weeks ago during your visit), and I paid another €50 (and will pay more for another visit). You can do an internet search, which says the same thing: Acular eye drops can slow down the healing process and even cause other problems (photo attached). I can give you the new ophthalmologist's number so he can confirm this over the phone.

In 15 days with the eye drops you recommended, nothing has changed. Since we stopped the Acular – which, I repeat, both an ophthalmologist and someone with no veterinary experience, like the internet, say can slow ulcer healing – and gave a different eye drop, the ulcer started to close in two days. Mistakes happen, so admit yours. And I agree that I paid for a visit to a vet who didn't know how to treat the ulcer, even though you say it was superficial. I had to pay for another visit to your ophthalmologist, so he probably didn't know how to properly treat ulcers either. You say a culture is needed for Vigamox, but Kali had another ulcer in the past that you yourselves had treated with Vigamox without doing any culture. Bah!
